newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise values media assets 5 bln - paper.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise values media assets 5 bln - paper.

text.p: French utilities and water company Lyonnaise des Eaux values its assets in the media and communications area at more than five billion francs, deputy chairman Guy de Panafieu said in a newspaper on Tuesday.

"Taking into account these figures, with our share in TPS (Television par Satellite), our assets in communications are worth more than five billion francs after investment of two billion francs," he said in an interview with La Tribune.
The M6 television station, in which Lyonnaise holds 34 percent, is valued at six billion, and Lyonnaise has a total 500,000 cable TV subscribers, he said.
A cable network is valued at 3,000 francs per connection on an international scale, he said. Lyonnaise has 400,000 individual cable subscribers and 100,000 on a communal connection.
"Development will continue," he said. "The television sector and cable services should represent between five and 10 percent of turnover of Lyonnaise des Eaux in 2005," he said.

Lyonnaise is a 10 percent shareholder in the TPS digital satellite joint venture which is being launched in competition to Canal Plus. Other TPS partners are TF1, state-owned France Television, M6 and Luxembourg's CLT, controlled by holding company Audiofina.
Lyonnaise des Eaux holds its media interests in the Lyonnaise Communications company, in which it owns 70 percent, with France Telecom holding 17 percent and US West with six percent.
